concerns.text: Phase 6 (T060-T069) introduces extensive feature engineering (conformational ensembles, thermodynamic context, rule discovery) not present in spec.md or plan.md. This constitutes unapproved scope creep that violates the spec's defined feature set and risks violating SC-005 (6-hour runtime) without a corresponding spec update. Tasks must not silently relax or expand constraints.

Task T051 introduces a fallback mechanism to reduce permutation shuffles from 10,000 to 1,000 if runtime limits are approached. This directly contradicts FR-016 and US-2 which mandate exactly 10,000 shuffles for statistical resolution. A task that allows a deliverable (p-value) to fall short of the FR's hard constraint is a constraint violation.

Task T009 claims to update plan.md to set CAPE as the target, but the provided plan.md Summary still explicitly states 'PC_raw is the target'. The task's deliverable (the updated plan) is not reflected in the artifact, indicating a failure to satisfy the spec's FR-011 (CAPE as target) and creating a semantic conflict between the task claim and the plan reality.

Task T028 describes partial-correlation analysis but omits the explicit requirement to 'report the adjusted correlation coefficient' in the final output as mandated by FR-014. The task description focuses on the method (one-hot encoding) but fails to ensure the specific deliverable (the reported value) is produced, risking a dropped acceptance criterion.

Task T057 states it will 'Validate SC-004 for the single model', but SC-004 requires demonstrating robustness across the high-packing thresholds {0.5, 0.6, 0.7}. The task description implies a single-model check rather than the required sensitivity analysis (sweeping thresholds), which is a semantic weakening of the acceptance criterion.
